steps.content: You return to the main hall to find small dinner tables already arranged. The meal itself is a testament to the times—a simple, ration-conscious spread of cold cuts and humble homestyle dishes. The only luxury is the wine: several bottles of a fine vintage, which Manphist is pouring into each guest's glass.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Ah, look who's back. Our brave ${PlayerName}.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: I am Manphis Gesso. Formerly of the cryptography department... now retired. Though most who know me usually call me "Manphist." Please, allow me to propose a toast!

You accept the wine glass from Manphist. As the others begin their introductions, their gazes linger on you. It's clear that the earlier incident has made you the center of their calculating attention.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: Helene Meiser. I'm an operative in Intelligence, a "Hatter." As for my job, well, I conduct... "in-depth exchanges" with any DisCity official gracious enough to share their time.

steps.speaker: Casey
steps.content: Ahem... I'm Casey Abel. Head of the Tomorrow Post, as well as its chief editor and writer. My team and I are responsible for "crafting" various exclusive news stories. We ensure the public receives the narrative precisely as we intend.

steps.speaker: Casey
steps.content: This is Mr. Johnson Madison. He also happens to be the handler who brought me on board.

steps.speaker: Johnson
steps.content: A pleasure, Mr. ${PlayerName}. I typically operate in the metropoles, so I don't find myself in DisCity often. I serve as the Personnel Director at the Economic Intelligence Center.
steps.female_content: A pleasure, Ms. ${PlayerName}. I typically operate in the metropoles, so I don't find myself in DisCity often. I serve as the Personnel Director at the Economic Intelligence Center.

steps.speaker: Huck
steps.content: Huck Burrows. Radio communications expert. Currently undercover as a technician at the West District power plant.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: Nolaine. I attend night school at Syndicate. My actual identity is an operative in the Cryptography Department. I report directly to Hilda.
Finally, the only one left is Marlo, who previously confronted you. He gives a cold snort.

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: Marlo Bannings. Killing's what I do.
His foul mood is a palpable force in the room, casting an immediate awkwardness over the group. It's Manphist who finally cuts the tension with a well-timed cough.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Pay him no mind. Marlo is an agent in our Operations Department. He specializes in handling... delicate matters. The sort best kept from the public eye.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Now then, since everyone is acquainted, let us take our seats and raise our glasses, to this rare gathering!
(Transition, still the same scene)
Amid the gentle clinking of glasses and the murmur of dinner conversation, you slip effortlessly into the spies' discussions.

steps.speaker: Johnson
steps.content: Dreadful weather. You can't get a letter through, let alone a clean radio signal. Hilda certainly picked a charming spot for us.

steps.speaker: Johnson
steps.content: I dread to think what state the markets will be in by the time I get back.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: If I recall, the private equity fund you manage is doing quite well. Several acquisition partnerships with local DisCity companies, is it not? I'm sure it will all be fine.

steps.speaker: Johnson
steps.content: It's the times we live in... Everyone just wants to park their wealth somewhere safe to ride out the war...

steps.speaker: Johnson
steps.content: We've already secured the daily supply lines. Now we're negotiating for energy and finance... Natives here are shrewd, but it doesn't matter. DisCity is desperate for capital; they won't refuse a good deal.

steps.speaker: Johnson
steps.content: Ms. Casey has been an immense help. Just a few of her news pieces kept the antitrust regulators tied up in knots. Absolutely brilliant work.
A smile touches his lips as he raises his glass in a tribute to Casey. She answers with a grin of self-satisfied triumph.

steps.speaker: Casey
steps.content: Just a few small favors. Mr. Johnson is the one with the sharp eye, always picking "quality companies" with such... manageable histories. They're easy to tidy up.

steps.speaker: Johnson
steps.content: Economic development is an invisible empire. When everything in this city-state, from dawn to dusk—the bread people eat, the fuel they burn, the news they watch, the pensions they save—is tied to us... That is true "market penetration."

steps.speaker: Johnson
steps.content: Trust me, that day is not far off.
The glasses meet with a crisp chime, a sound as fragile and transient as the beautiful dreams they now toast.
He, of course, is blissfully unaware that his own downfall is already circling. You alone know the history that is about to unfold, and you keep your face a perfect, neutral mask.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, you've barely touched your food. Is it not to your liking? I could have the chef prepare a stew for you instead.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's nothing. I was just spacing out for a moment.

You spear a piece of cold meat with your fork just as the conversation deftly pivots. It's clear they're avoiding revealing too much about themselves, skillfully steering the topic back to the safer ground of Monolith and Hilda.

steps.speaker: Huck
steps.content: So... why did Edward have to die? Hilda just executed him like that... How is she going to explain it to the superiors?

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Well, strictly speaking, Edward was planning to commit suicide. Hilda only intended to question him, so the blame can't be laid at her feet. Horne's death, however, is more complicated...

steps.speaker: Casey
steps.content: Horne mentioned earlier that Hilda's parents defected to DisCity. Is that true?
Helene raises a finger to her lips, her smile a deliberate and mysterious curve.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: Oh, you must be new. The Hartleins' defection was a major scandal in Sevael. One is a city-state councilor, the other a media tycoon. Plenty were sent to apprehend them, but they slipped through the net regardless.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: Rumor has it they were highly valued after arriving in DisCity. Lavish banquets, luxurious estates... probably not unlike where we are now.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: A pity for Hilda, though. She was implicated and placed on "the list," which made it impossible for her to remain in the metropoles. She fled to the DisCity front line and had to claw her way up from the bottom to reach her current position.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: Monolith is her passion project, and her pledge of loyalty to the metropoles. If it succeeds, she can return to the city-state, and her ascent will be assured.

steps.speaker: Casey
steps.content: So that's why she hates the mole so much... She's using our lives as stepping stones for her own promotion!

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: Hmph. Sounds like someone's conscience is acting up?

steps.speaker: Casey
steps.content: No, no, no... I just think it's all too reckless... After all, we're all on the same side... we're colleagues, right?
As if she has told the most wonderful joke, the room erupts in laughter. The sound is almost too loud, too unified, weaving an atmosphere of eerily forced cheer.
After dinner, shifts are assigned by a draw of lots, and everyone takes turns returning to their quarters to rest.

Your room is a makeshift archive, crammed with towers of old books and files that reach from the floor to the ceiling. A quick inspection reveals they are not classified, but rather mundane academic texts.
A sparse military cot is wedged into the corner, your only concession to comfort for the night.
You recall that Hilda's room is right next door... Before even thinking of rest, you begin a systematic sweep for any surveillance devices.
